column1: # Moves a line's own note names as the answer to a threat, but which the
# ordinary top-five search never reports. Without a number here the note is
# asserting something the shipped table cannot support.
# hip-150, the Be3/Qd2/f3/g4 storm tabiya. Its note prescribes three counters,
# ...h5, ...c5 and ...d5. Only ...h5 is in the stored five (best, -68); the
# other two were in neither list, so both graded "unknown" and setupGate could
# say nothing about them. W1-D raised this; these two entries answer it.
# The Greek gift in the Koltanowski clamp position (kolt ply 22). syn-greek used
# to drill 12.Bxh7+ here, which is why the row carries it; the line is gone, so
# force it explicitly or a regeneration would drop the -269 that justifies the
# The storm tabiya after 5.h4: alternatives the notes name, so each carries a number.
# The storm tabiya after 5.g4: alternatives the notes name, so each carries a number.
# Break or capture: the three structural choices the notes now state as numbers
# rather than rules. ck ply 18 (after 10...Qc7): e5 at once, against the exchange
# the table prefers. kolt ply 20 (after 11...Re8): the exchange exd5, against the
# e5 clamp it prefers. hip66 ply 21 (after d5 with c4 in): the capture ...exd5,
# against the ...e5 lock; syn-hipc5 is the same push without c4, where it flips.
# Counted player choices the ranked five do not contain (tools/count-choices.mjs
# --tsv, from research/choices-player.json). Each was chosen in at least 5% of at least 30
# games reaching the position in one rating band, and at least 10 times, so
# the app may name it as a common choice; it needs a score before it may be
# priced. 68 moves at 31 positions. 25 more sit at positions that already
# have a forced search, which this section must not change; they stay unscored.
